label: prf:frobenius-relation
title: Proof of Frobenius relation
html:
The Frobenius form \int_A and the multiplication \mu together define a non-degenerate pairing \langle a, b \rangle = \int_A(\mu(a \otimes b)) (Frobenius pairing), giving an isomorphism \phi \colon A \xrightarrow{\sim} A^{\vee}. Define the dual comultiplication \Delta_\mu as the transpose of \mu under \phi:

  \Delta_\mu = (\phi^{-1} \otimes \phi^{-1}) \circ \mu^{\vee} \circ \phi.

To verify the Frobenius relation, the two composites (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta_\mu) and \Delta_\mu \circ \mu are maps A \otimes A \to A \otimes A; by non-degeneracy it suffices to show they agree after pairing with an arbitrary test element c \in A. Writing \Delta_\mu(b) = b_1 \otimes b_2 in Sweedler notation, the left-hand side equals

  \int_A \mu\bigl(\mu(a \otimes b_1) \otimes b_2\bigr) \cdot c
  = \int_A \mu\bigl(a \otimes \mu(b_1 \otimes b_2)\bigr) \cdot c

by associativity of \mu, and the right-hand side equals \int_A \mu(a \otimes \mu(b_1 \otimes b_2)) \cdot c directly. Both sides agree, so the Frobenius relation holds: \Delta_\mu is the transpose of \mu, and associativity of \mu is the only non-trivial axiom used. \square
